{{Quote|The Kashi Guardians of Breath still persist, despite the ancient destruction of their homeworld by a supernova.|Restelly Quist, ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force''|<ref name="JP" />}}
The '''Guardians of the Breath''', also known as the '''Kashi Mer Mystics''', was an organization of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] hailing from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashi]]. Possessing a strong connection to the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]], they used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]&mdash;known as "the Breath" to the [[Kashi Mer]] culture which they served&mdash;to [[Plant Surge|aid]] with growing [[Plant/Legends|crops]] and [[Force healing/Legends|healing]] the sick and injured. At some point by [[24,500 BBY]], the [[Kashi system]] was destroyed by a [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]]; however, the Guardians survived the disaster, albeit with its members becoming scattered. The organization was still in existence by [[990 BBY]] when it was briefly described in the [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi trainee]] [[Book/Legends|guidebook]] ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''.

==Description==
{{Quote|Blessed with a strong connection to the Living Force, their scattered members can stimulate remarkable surges in the cell growth of both plants and animals.|Restelly Quist, ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force''|<ref name="JP" />}}
[[File:Kashi-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Guardians of the Breath served the Kashi Mer culture of the planet Kashi.]]
The Guardians of the Breath,<ref name="TotJC" /> also known as the Kashi Mer Mystics,<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> was an organization of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]]. They drew upon [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], which was known as "the Breath" to the [[Kashi Mer]] culture,<ref name="TotJC" /> to cause significant surges in the cell growth of [[Plant Surge|plants]] and animals.<ref name="JP" /> The Guardians in turn used such effects to provide aid with the growing of [[Plant/Legends|crops]] and the [[Force healing/Legends|healing]] of sick and injured individuals. In addition, the group known as the [[Guardian Elders]] interpreted [[Force vision/Legends|visions]] received via the Breath to inform the Kashi Mer civilization on the path that it should follow. The Guardians also maintained the lore of the Breath as well as its usage methods, passing the knowledge down by oral tradition as recording it in any format was considered to be blasphemous.<ref name="TotJC" />

Tens of thousands of Kashi Mer, who worshipped the Breath for its life-giving power, applied [[Standard year/Legends|annually]] for membership in the hierarchy of the Guardians of the Breath; however,<ref name="TotJC" /> despite the fact that many members of the culture in general possessed the innate ability to<ref name="CSWE KashiMer">{{CSWECite|II|201|Kashi Mer}}</ref> access the Breath, frequently less than a handful of the applicants had that ability. The Guardian initiates then progressed through several levels of Attainment and learning about the lore of the Breath and the powers it granted. As most Guardians eventually discovered a limit to their understanding and control over the Breath, fewer and fewer candidates remained at each stage of advancement through the organization's structure.<ref name="TotJC" /> In general, however, the members of the tradition exhibited a strong attunement to the Force aspect known as the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]]. At least one Guardian of the Breath was [[Human/Legends|Human]], and they [[Clothing/Legends|wore]] a dark-[[Color/Legends|gray]] [[Robe/Legends|robe]] with a hood as well as a piece of red-and-gold fabric across their left shoulder.<ref name="JP" />

Over the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] of their existence, the Guardians of the Breath [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] several members, sentencing them to wandering [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] worldless for the rest of their lives. Some of the exiles began using the Breath for self-gain and the destruction of other individuals, and travelers who had encountered such former Guardians subsequently tended to avoid meeting any members of the tradition whatsoever.<ref name="TotJC" />

==History==
{{Quote|Fascinating!|Qui-Gon Jinn's annotation in his copy of ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force''|<ref name="JP" />}}
[[File:Young_qui-gon.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The Jedi Qui-Gon Jinn was fascinated by the description of the Force abilities of the Guardians of the Breath.]]
The Guardians of the Breath hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="JP" /> [[Kashi]], originating with its<ref name="TotJC" /> [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]]-old Kashi Mer culture.<ref name="Journal6">{{JournalCite|6|Relic (article)}}</ref> After the organization had existed for years,<ref name="TotJC" /> its members became scattered<ref name="JP" /> at some point by [[24,500 BBY]]<ref name="24500BBY" /> when the [[Kashi system]] was suddenly destroyed by an inexplicable [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] that largely rendered the Kashi Mer extinct.<ref name="Journal6" />

The Guardians still existed<ref name="JP" /> by [[990 BBY]],<ref name="990 BBY">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/12/endnotes-for-star-wars-jedi-path-part-1.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Jedi Path (part 1 of 4)|quote=Okay, so we've established that this particular copy of the book dates from 115 BBY. But the content inside is [&hellip;] dating from the year 990 BBY.}}</ref> when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Chief Librarian/Legends|Chief Librarian]] [[Restelly Quist/Legends|Restelly Quist]] briefly mentioned them in a section of the [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi trainee]] [[Book/Legends|guidebook]] ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'' focusing on Force-using traditions other than those of the Jedi and their antithesis, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. In the passage, Quist characterized the Guardians' connection to the Living Force as a blessing. At some point between [[82 BBY]] and [[72 BBY/Legends|72 BBY]], in his copy of book, the Jedi [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]<ref name="JP" />&mdash;who eventually himself developed a strong attunement to the Living Force<ref name="CSWE Jinn">{{CSWECite|II|164|Jinn, Qui-Gon}}</ref>&mdash;underlined Quist's description of the Guardians' Force abilities and noted in an annotation his fascination with them.<ref name="JP" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tales_of_the_Jedi_Companion.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Guardians of the Breath were introduced in the ''Tales of the Jedi Companion''.]]
The Guardians of the Breath were first mentioned in the [[1996]] [[roleplaying game]] sourcebook ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'', written by [[George R. Strayton]] and published by [[West End Games]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="TotJC" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], introduced the alternate name "Kashi Mer Mystics" for the organization.<ref name="TEA" />

The ''Tales of the Jedi Companion'' introduces a contradiction regarding the dating of the Kashi [[Star system/Legends|system's]] destruction<ref name="TotJC" />&mdash;and therefore the fragmentation of the Guardians of the Breath<ref name="JP" />&mdash;with Strayton's earlier work, the roleplaying adventure "[[Relic (article)|Relic]]," which was published in the [[May]] [[1995]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 6|sixth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine.<ref name="Journal6" /> Set approximately 4,000 years before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the former work presents information on the Kashi system, including a description of the Guardians' activities therein, as if it still existed at that time.<ref name="TotJC" /> This conflicts with "Relic" stating that the system had been destroyed shortly after the formation of the Galactic Republic<ref name="Journal6" />&mdash;an event that had already been established by 1996 to have occurred around twenty-five millennia before the events of ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Guide2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> This article therefore assumes that the information from the ''Tales of the Jedi Companion'' regarding the Kashi system instead applies to the time period preceding its destruction.
